Subject: RE: production errors & slowdowns (last 36h)

Ben / John — quick tech summary from infra:

- Root cause: a scheduling regression in our dedicated routing layer combined with an upstream GPU driver patch that increased tail latency for rwd-medium quantized instances when client concurrency exceeded ~320 QPS.
- Scope: affects about 4 of ThunderBay's reserved shards between 2026-07-24T03:10Z and 2026-07-25T22:45Z (approx 41 hours).
- Impact: 5xx rate spike to 3.8% on average (baseline <0.1%), median per-token latency rose from 72ms -> 190ms, tail (p95-p99) spiked to 1.2s.

Remediation steps taken: reverted scheduling change (rolled back 2026-07-26 02:00Z), applied a targeted driver fallback to affected hosts, and rebalanced ThunderBay shards to mitigated nodes. Error rate and latency are back within SLA ranges as of 2026-07-26 14:00Z.

Commercial thought: based on your committed monthly throughput and the 41-hour window of elevated impact, an industry-standard make-good is around 8-12% of that month's committed invoice for the affected capacity. I can run a detailed calc once we cross-check consumed tokens and your reserved units.

I'll follow up with the exact token counts and a proposed credit table this afternoon.

-M

Marissa Cole
Head of Incident Response, Redwood Inference

John / Karen — thanks for elevating this. I’m looping in legal and finance to expedite. Proposed commercial settlement (initial):

- One-time credit equal to 10% of ThunderBay's July 2026 reserved capacity charge (reflects the 41-hour SLA breach window and observed uplift in error/latency).
- Credit applied to the Aug 2026 invoice; if August invoice does not cover the full credit, remaining balance will be issued as account credit.
- Operational commitment: dedicated placement policy exemption for ThunderBay shards and a 60-day verification window where we will provide weekly telemetry reports and two joint runbooks (placement & driver rollback).
- Contract amendment: a short SOW addendum that documents the credit and the verification steps; legal will push a DocuSign link within 24 hours.

We intend this to be a swift fix — we recognize the commercial impact and want to avoid protracted back-and-forth. If this is acceptable, Ben will send the DocuSign and I’ll authorize the credit accounting work.
